cfpb-renthelp.name: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rent help page
cfpb-renthelp.outcome: Points renters to state, tribal, and local rental assistance, 211, HUD-approved housing counselors, year-round utility help through LIHEAP (the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program), and housing choice vouchers
cfpb-renthelp.limits: A directory, not money itself; local assistance funds vary by place and often run out.
cfpb-renthelp.locator: "State, tribal, and local organizations are the best place to start."

hud-vouchers.name: Housing Choice Voucher program (Section 8)
hud-vouchers.outcome: About 2,000 local public housing agencies run it with HUD funding; the family typically pays about 30% of adjusted monthly income, up to 40%, and the agency pays the landlord the rest
hud-vouchers.limits: For extremely low and very low incomes; waiting lists are often long, so people apply to several agencies.
hud-vouchers.locator: Section on the tenant's share: Total Tenant Payment about 30% of adjusted income

rent-negotiation-avail.name: Avail survey of renters negotiating rent
rent-negotiation-avail.outcome: Success rate for negotiating lower rent rose from 17% in October 2022 to just over 25% in April 2023; only 28% negotiated their most recent renewal
rent-negotiation-avail.limits: Secondary source (a CNBC story republished by NBC Bay Area) reporting a survey by Avail, a landlord and tenant platform; the 2023 rate reflects a cooling market. Tips given: compare local listings, cite on-time payment history, offer a longer lease such as two years, time the lease for December or January, or ask for repairs or waived fees instead.
rent-negotiation-avail.locator: Headline: "1 in 4 Renters Are Successfully Negotiating Lower Prices"

tulsa-remote.name: Tulsa Remote
tulsa-remote.outcome: A $10,000 grant for remote workers who move to Tulsa for a year; more than 3,300 workers since 2019, about 90% stay longer than a year; one participant's mortgage on a three-bedroom home roughly equals what she paid for a single room in Los Angeles
tulsa-remote.limits: Secondary news report using program-supplied figures; only for people whose job is already remote. Funded mainly by the George Kaiser Family Foundation. Moving costs and leaving people behind are real costs.
tulsa-remote.locator: "Tulsa Remote is a one-year program that offers a $10,000 grant"

pew-multigenerational.name: Pew Research Center on multigenerational homes
pew-multigenerational.outcome: Among adults 25 and older living with a parent, 57% of those ages 25 to 39 say finances are a major reason, compared with 31% of older adults
pew-multigenerational.limits: A survey of why people live together, not a measure of how much they save; living with family isn't possible or safe for everyone.
pew-multigenerational.locator: "much more likely than older ones to say this (57% to 31%)"

aarp-golden-girls.name: Older women sharing homes as housemates (AARP report)
aarp-golden-girls.outcome: 57% of women 50 and older would consider living with a friend as they age (2024 AARP survey); about 1 in 4 adults 50 and older would consider renting part of their home to a nonfamily member (July 2026); Colorado's 2024 law removed local caps on unrelated people living together
aarp-golden-girls.limits: Willingness in surveys, not how many actually do it; only 6% would consider living with a stranger.
aarp-golden-girls.locator: Title: "Could You Really Live Like the 'Golden Girls'?"

nesterly.name: Nesterly home-sharing matches
nesterly.outcome: Matches people who have spare rooms with renters for stays of a month or more; guests can agree to help around the home in exchange for lower rent; either side can end with 30 days' notice
nesterly.limits: Company's own description; availability depends on hosts in your area.
nesterly.locator: "Share a home with someone you can trust"

homeshare-vermont.name: HomeShare Vermont
homeshare-vermont.outcome: Nonprofit matching housemates since 1982 across 12 of Vermont's 14 counties; people choose whom they live with after screening
homeshare-vermont.limits: Vermont only; the home page doesn't state rent or fees. AARP reports that the average host is 71, the average guest 42, and rent can't exceed $650 a month, which wasn't confirmed on HomeShare Vermont's own page.
homeshare-vermont.locator: Home page: matching service operating since 1982

kc-tenants-independence-towers.name: KC Tenants rent strike at Independence Towers
kc-tenants-independence-towers.outcome: After an eight-month rent strike, tenants won a contract that held rents steady, removed some extra fees, and set a deadline for repairs; KC Tenants, founded in 2019, has more than 10,000 members
kc-tenants-independence-towers.limits: Secondary news source; a rent strike carries eviction risk and works best with many tenants and legal backing.

champlain-housing-trust.name: Champlain Housing Trust shared-equity homes
champlain-housing-trust.outcome: Study of 205 resales of homes developed 1988 to 2008: the average seller left nearly $14,000 richer after about 5.4 years, and 73% bought another home when they left
champlain-housing-trust.limits: Secondary source (New America) summarizing a study; sellers keep only part of the appreciation, so it builds less wealth than a market-rate home in a hot market.

vienna-city-flats.name: Vienna city-owned and co-operative flats
vienna-city-flats.outcome: About 220,000 city-owned flats and 200,000 co-operative flats; eligibility needs two years living in Vienna and income below a limit
vienna-city-flats.limits: Built over about a century; newcomers must wait and meet eligibility rules, and city flats also require a qualifying need such as overcrowding.

montgomery-hoc.name: Housing Opportunities Commission mixed-income social housing
montgomery-hoc.outcome: The county housing agency set up a Housing Production Fund in 2021 to build mixed-income apartments it owns; the first, The Laureate, has 268 homes, with affordable and market-rate homes looking the same and higher rents offsetting lower ones
montgomery-hoc.limits: Secondary source (Dezeen); the page doesn't give the fund's size or the share of affordable units, and the model is young.
montgomery-hoc.locator: Section on The Laureate, the fund's first completed project with 268 homes

minneapolis-reforms.name: Minneapolis land-use reforms
minneapolis-reforms.outcome: From 2017 to 2022 the city permitted about 21,000 new homes, about 12% more housing against about 4% statewide, and rent growth ran 13 percentage points below the state average; renters pay about $1,700 a year less than if rents had tracked the state
minneapolis-reforms.limits: Secondary report of a Pew Charitable Trusts analysis (Pew's page blocked the fetch). Reforms included ending parking minimums, allowing duplexes and triplexes on every lot, and apartments along transit; the duplex rule had a modest effect so far.
minneapolis-reforms.locator: "rent growth in the city is 13 percentage points lower than the state average"

oregon-rent-cap.name: Oregon statewide rent stabilization
oregon-rent-cap.outcome: Yearly rent increases are capped at 7% plus inflation, never more than 10%; the cap was 9.5% for 2026 and is 10% for 2027
oregon-rent-cap.limits: A ceiling on increases, not a rent cut; the cap is high enough that it mostly stops the biggest jumps. Exemptions such as new construction aren't stated on this page.
oregon-rent-cap.locator: "the maximum allowable rent increase percentage for tenancies subject to ORS 90.324(b) is 10%"

sf-rent-control-study.name: Stanford study of San Francisco's 1994 rent control expansion
sf-rent-control-study.outcome: Covered tenants saved roughly $2,300 to $6,600 a year, but rent-controlled units fell about 25% from 1994 to 2010 and later renters paid about 5% more
sf-rent-control-study.limits: One city and one era; economists and tenant advocates disagree on what it means for other rent rules. Secondary write-up of the research by Stanford's business school.
sf-rent-control-study.locator: "we don't provide any formal insurance against rent increases"

nyc-right-to-counsel.name: New York City right to counsel in eviction cases
nyc-right-to-counsel.outcome: 89% of tenants with full legal representation in an eviction case in fiscal 2024 stayed stably housed; citywide representation fell from 71% in fiscal 2021 to 42% in fiscal 2024
nyc-right-to-counsel.limits: Protects against eviction rather than lowering rent; there aren't enough lawyers to meet the promise.
nyc-right-to-counsel.locator: Comptroller release: 89% of fully represented tenants remained stably housed

brooke-amendment.name: Brooke Amendment, origin of the 30% rent rule
brooke-amendment.outcome: Capped public housing rent at 25% of a tenant's income in 1969; raised to 30% in 1981, which became the common rule of thumb for affordable rent
brooke-amendment.limits: Secondary source (an encyclopedia); the cap applies only to public housing, and the 30% figure is a convention, not a measured threshold.
brooke-amendment.locator: "capped rent in public housing projects at 25% of tenant's income"

germany-rent-brake.name: Conny and Germany's rent brake
germany-rent-brake.outcome: In tight markets, rent on a new lease may be no more than 10% above the local comparative rent from the city's rent index; Conny checks a tenant's rent, sends the formal complaint, and charges only if the rent is reduced
germany-rent-brake.limits: Company's own description; German law only, with exceptions such as new builds first rented after 1 October 2014. Overpaid rent is reclaimed only from the complaint date, with longer windows for some newer leases.
germany-rent-brake.locator: "no more than 10% above the local comparative rent"

justfix.name: JustFix tenant tools
justfix.outcome: Free tools to order an apartment's rent history by mail or text, look up who owns a building and their other properties (Who Owns What), and send a repair letter by certified mail
justfix.limits: New York City only; rent history matters most for rent-stabilized apartments.
justfix.locator: "Exercise your rights by sending a customized letter to your landlord"

la-adus.name: Backyard homes (ADUs) in Los Angeles
la-adus.outcome: Over 25,000 accessory dwelling units (backyard homes) permitted in the city since 2017, after California made them easier to build
la-adus.limits: Secondary news source citing Crosstown LA; a permit isn't a finished home, and building one needs a homeowner with land and money.
la-adus.locator: "Over 25,000 ADUs have been permitted in LA since 2017."
